summary: Junko Matsumura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed an MA at the Australian National University by 1980 and a doctoral dissertation at the University of Göttingen by 1990, later serving as professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Junko Minamoto works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed a master's program at Ryukoku University, withdrew upon completing coursework for a doctoral program at Otani University, and held a commissioned researcher post at Kansai University.
Junko Sakamoto-Gotō works in Indology and linguistics. She held posts at Tohoku University (attested 2005) and Ryukoku University (attested 2015).

Junmai Zhang (1886–1969) was a scholar of philosophy and sinology. He studied under Qichao Liang, at Waseda University, and at Humboldt University of Berlin. He later held posts at Peking University and Tsinghua University.

Junsho Kato is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo, KU Leuven, and under Akira Hirakawa, Hajime Nakamura, Juntaka Kato, and Étienne Lamotte. He held professorships at Nishogakusha University and Nagoya University.

Juntarō Ishihama (1888–1968) was a scholar of sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. After studying at Kansai University, he held posts at Ryukoku University (~1921–1948) and Kansai University (~1934–1968).
Junzo Inagaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Shoshin Fukihara. He served as a section chief at Otani University.
Juri Lotman (1922–1993) was a scholar of linguistics and philosophy. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and held a post at the University of Tartu beginning in 1954.
Juro Watanabe is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Gerhard Oberhammer. He held a post at the University of Tsukuba (attested 1989–1990).

Justin McDaniel is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of California, Riverside, and as an endowed humanities professor at the University of Pennsylvania.

Justin Ritzinger works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Michael Puett, and held posts at Dharma Drum Mountain, Oberlin College, Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts, and Academia Sinica.
Justin Shimeld is a scholar of philosophy. He completed a PhD at the University of Tasmania, where he studied under doctoral supervisors Jeff Malpas and Sonam Thakchoe.
Justus Günther Grassmann (1779–1852) studied at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1797–1801) and held a post at the Marienstiftsgymnasium from 1806 to 1852.

Justus Olshausen (1800–1882) was a scholar in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Kiel, Berlin, and Paris, holding posts at Kiel University, the University of Königsberg, the Prussian Academy of Sciences, and the Ministry of Spiritual Affairs.
Jyotirindranath Tagore (1849–1925) was active in Indology and other fields. He studied at Hindu School and Presidency University.

János Szerb (1951–1988) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Eötvös Loránd University (~1974–1980), he held posts at the University of Vienna and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.
Jérôme Ducor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Jacques May and held an affiliation at the University of Lausanne (~2005–2011).

Józef Szczepan Kowalewski (1800–1878) worked in Iranian/Central Asian and Buddhist studies. Educated at Vilnius and Kazan under scholars including Groddeck and Erdmann, he became professor and rector at Kazan University before serving as professor and dean at the University of Warsaw.
Józef Turczyński (1884–1953) held posts at the Ukrainian National Academy of Music (~1915–1919) and the Chopin University of Music (~1920–1939), and he taught Constantin Regamey.

József Budenz (1836–1892) was a linguist who studied at the University of Marburg and under Theodor Benfey at the University of Göttingen. He served at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences and as professor of Altaic comparative linguistics at Eötvös Loránd University.
